record.title: Babson–Reiner connectivity conjecture for Coxeter-like complexes
record.statement: Let $T$ be a tree with $n$ nodes and $b$ leaves, and let $cDelta_T$ be its Coxeter-like complex. **Babson–Reiner conjecture.** The complex $cDelta_T$ is at least $(n-1-b)$-connected. The paper states that this conjecture is proved in its Theorem, so it is solved; it generalizes connectivity results for chessboard complexes and type A Coxeter complexes.
record.source_name: Patricia Hersh, “Shelling Coxeter-like Complexes and Sorting on Trees”, arXiv:0809.2414 (2008).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0809.2414

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of September 2008); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: The order conjecture for spanning-tree recurrences of grid graphs
record.statement: Let $G_k(n)$ denote the grid graph considered in the paper, with the recurrence for its spanning-tree counts taken with respect to $n$. **Grid recurrence order conjecture.** The recurrence for the grid graph $G_k(n)$ has order $2^{k-1}$. This predicts an exact recurrence order for the spanning-tree sequence of the grid graphs; the source provides no evidence of resolution.

record.title: Lei Zhou's ternary Goldbach-type conjecture
record.statement:
Let $p_1$ and $p_2$ be odd primes. **Lei Zhou's conjecture.** Every odd integer $n\geq9$ can be represented in the form

$$
n=p_1+2p_2.
$$

This is presented as a strengthening of the ternary Goldbach problem and is attributed to Lei Zhou; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Vladimir Shevelev, “On Unique Additive Representations of Positive Integers and Some Close Problems”, arXiv:0811.0290 (2008).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.0290

record.title: Narayana distribution conjecture for path lengths of 231-avoiding permutations
record.statement:
Let $S_n(231)$ denote the set of $231$-avoiding permutations of $[n]$. For $\pi\in S_n(231)$, let $\operatorname{pathlen}(\pi)$ be the length of the path corresponding to $\pi$ under the construction above, and let $N(n,k)$ be a Narayana number.

**Narayana distribution conjecture.** The path lengths have the Narayana distribution:

$$
\sum_{\pi \in S_n(231)} q^{\operatorname{pathlen}(\pi)} = q^{2n} \sum_{k \ge 0} N(n,k)q^{2k}.
$$

Moreover,

$$
\sum_{n \ge 0}\sum_{\pi \in S_n(231)}q^{\operatorname{pathlen}(\pi)} = \frac{1-q^2+q^4-\sqrt{1-2q^2-q^4-2q^6+q^8}}{2q^4}.
$$

The conjecture identifies the length statistic arising from the bijective construction with the Narayana distribution and gives its bivariate generating function. The paper presents this as an observed pattern supported by computations; no proof or resolution is supplied here.
record.source_name: Dan Drake, “Bijections from weighted Dyck paths to Schroeder paths”, arXiv:1006.1959 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.1959

record.title: Nonexistence of a finite planar fair-win goal set
record.statement: In the planar achievement game, a finite point set $G\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ is used as the goal set: players alternately place points, and Player 1 seeks to build a congruent copy of $G$ before Player 2 does. A **fair win** is a win in which Player 1 builds a goal set on a turn preceding every turn on which Player 2 builds one. **Planar fair-win nonexistence conjecture.** There is no finite point set $G\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ for which Player 1 has a strategy ensuring a fair win in the $G$-achievement game played in the plane. The preceding examples show that fair wins can occur for finite hypergraphs, but the claim asserts that no finite planar point set has this property.
record.source_name: Wesley Pegden, “A finite goal set in the plane which is not a Winner”, arXiv:1101.4420 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.4420

record.title: Characterization of extremal incomplete sets in cyclic groups of order $pq$
record.statement:
Let $p,q$ be two odd prime numbers and let $G=Z_{pq}$. Write ${\rm cr}(G)$ for the critical number of $G$, and call a subset **incomplete** when its subset sums do not cover $G$. Assume

$$
p<q\leq p+\lfloor2\sqrt{p-2}\rfloor+1,
$$

$|A|={\rm cr}(G)-1=p+q-2$, and $0\notin A$.

**Extremal-set conjecture.** There exists an element $g\in G$ of order $pq$ such that

$$
A=\{\pm g,\pm 2g,\ldots,\pm \frac{p+q-2}{2}g\}.
$$

This conjecture proposes a classification of the extremal incomplete sets in the stated range. The source gives no resolution, so its status remains open.
record.source_name: Dan Guo, Yongke Qu, Guoqing Wang and Qinghong Wang, “Extremal incomplete sets in finite abelian groups”, arXiv:1101.4715 (2011).

record.title: Disk minimization conjecture for convex-domain Neumann eigenvalue sums
record.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a convex domain of given diameter $D$, and let $0=\mu_1(\Omega)<\mu_2(\Omega)\leq\mu_3(\Omega)\leq\cdots$ be the Neumann Laplacian eigenvalues. **Disk minimization conjecture.** For each integer $n\geq 3$, the scale-invariant sum

$$
\bigl(\mu_2(\Omega)+\dots+\mu_n(\Omega)\bigr)D^2
$$

is minimized when $\Omega$ is a disk. This is suggested by the proved result for triangular domains and the proposition for ellipses, but the assertion for general convex domains remains open.
record.source_name: R. S. Laugesen, Z. C. Pan and S. S. Son, “Neumann eigenvalue sums on triangles are (mostly) minimal for equilaterals”, arXiv:1102.0071 (2011).

record.title: The firefighter number conjecture for planar graphs of girth at least 5
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}_5$ be the class of planar graphs of girth at least $5$, and let $\mathit{ff}(\mathcal{P}_5)$ denote its firefighter number. **Firefighter number conjecture for planar graphs of girth at least 5.**

$$
\mathit{ff}(\mathcal{P}_5)=1.
$$

The paper explains that this would be stronger than the known result $\mathit{ff}(\mathcal{P}_9)=1$ and suggests adapting its proof techniques to the girth-$5$ case, but the conjecture remains open.

record.title: Maximal-coefficient conjecture for Stern polynomials
record.statement:
Let

$$
B_{n}(t)=\sum_{i=0}^{e(n)}a_{i,e(n)}x^{i}
$$

and define

$$
\mathcal{M}(n)=\operatorname{max}\{a_{i,e(n)}:\;i=1,2,\ldots,e(n)\}.
$$

Then the following equality holds:

$$
\operatorname{max}\{\mathcal{M}(m):\;m\in[2^{n-1},2^{n}]\}=\operatorname{max}\{C(n,0),C(n-1,1),\ldots,C(n-k,k)\},
$$

where $k$ is equal to $n/2$ if $n$ is even and $(n-1)/2$ if $n$ is odd.

This conjecture arose from investigations of the sequence of maximal coefficients of the Stern polynomial $B_n(t)$. The supplied context does not define the coefficient notation $a_{i,e(n)}$ or the quantities $C(n,j)$, so those definitions and the conjecture's current status should be checked against the source.
record.source_name: Maciej Ulas, “Arithmetic properties of the sequence of degrees of Stern polynomials and related results”, arXiv:1102.5111 (2011).

record.title: Pointed splitting subspace conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\alpha\in{\mathbb F}_{q^{mn}}$ satisfy

$$
{\mathbb F}_{q^{mn}}={\mathbb F}_q(\alpha),
$$

and let $x\in{\mathbb F}_{q^{mn}}^*$. An $m$-dimensional pointed $\alpha$-splitting subspace with base point $x$ is a pair $(W,x)$ where $W$ is an $m$-dimensional $\alpha$-splitting subspace and $x\in W$. **Pointed splitting subspace conjecture.** The number of $m$-dimensional pointed $\alpha$-splitting subspaces of ${\mathbb F}_{q^{mn}}$ with base point $x$ is

$$
q^{m(m-1)(n-1)}.
$$

The source states that this conjecture implies the earlier splitting-subspace and fiber conjectures, and that it is trivial when $m=1$ or $n=1$; it remains open in general.
record.source_name: Sudhir R. Ghorpade and Samrith Ram, “Block Companion Singer Cycles, Primitive Recursive Vector Sequences, and Coprime Polynomial Pairs over Finite Fields”, arXiv:1102.5335 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1102.5335

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2011). “As such the question about the enumeration of block companion Singer cycles over $\Fq$ is intimately related to the open problem about the determination of the total number of $\sigma$-splitting subspaces over $\Fq$ of a given dimension.”

record.title: Gács et al.'s prescribed-range polynomial conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field with $q=p^n$ elements, and let $M=\{a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_q\}$ be a multiset of $\mathbb{F}_q$ satisfying

$$
a_1+\cdots+a_q=0.
$$

A polynomial has **range** $M$ if its values on $\mathbb{F}_q$, counted with multiplicity, form $M$.

**Gács et al.'s conjecture.** Let $k<\sqrt{p}$. If no polynomial with range $M$ has degree less than $q-k$, then $M$ contains an element of multiplicity at least $q-k$.

The paper's abstract states that this conjecture is false over $\mathbb{F}_q$ for $p>9$ and $k=q-\ell-1\geq 3$, so the claim is refuted in the source paper.
record.source_name: Muratović-Ribić and Qiang Wang, “On a conjecture of polynomials with prescribed range”, arXiv:1103.3635 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1103.3635

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of March 2011); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Generalised squashed cube conjecture for exact clause-sets
record.statement:
Let $F$ be an **exact clause-set**, meaning that its deficiency is maximal among all clause-sets with the same conflict matrix or conflict multigraph. Suppose that the conflict matrix of $F$ is the distance matrix of a connected graph.

**Generalised squashed cube conjecture.** Then $F$ is matching lean.

This generalises the squashed cube conjecture, which was solved by Peter Winkler. Under the same assumptions, Winkler's original result is equivalent to $
\delta(F)\geq 1$ for non-empty $F$; the stronger matching-lean assertion is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Oliver Kullmann, “Constraint satisfaction problems in clausal form”, arXiv:1103.3693 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1103.3693

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2011). “This conjecture has been proven true in , using tools from matroid theory.”

record.title: Homotopy-equivalent topological representations detect isomorphisms of matroids
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a finite CW complex that is not contractible, and let $(M,l)$ and $(N,l')$ be $\rho$-immersed matroids such that

$$
{
\mathscr T}_X(M,l) \simeq {\mathscr T}_X(N,l').
$$

Suppose there exists a surjective weak map $\tau:M\to N$. **Topological representation isomorphism conjecture.** Then $\tau^{\#}$ is an isomorphism.

This conjecture proposes that, for a noncontractible base complex, homotopy equivalence of the associated topological representations forces the induced map on the relevant matroid data to be an isomorphism. The surrounding results establish strict Betti-number inequalities under rank-decreasing surjective weak maps, but the stated implication is not resolved here.
record.source_name: Matthew T. Stamps, “Topological representations of matroid maps”, arXiv:1104.4152 (2012).

record.title: Babson–Kozlov connectivity conjecture for Hom complexes
record.statement: Let $G$ be a graph with maximal degree $d$, and let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices. **Babson–Kozlov's conjecture.** The complex $\operatorname{Hom}(G,K_n)$ is at least $(n-d-2)$-connected. This conjecture was posed by Babson and Kozlov and is stated in the paper as a conjecture; the supplied material gives no resolution status.

record.title: Connectedness conjecture for least-perimeter disk partitions
record.statement: Let a **minimizing graph** be a least-perimeter partition of the unit disk into regions of prescribed areas. **Connectedness conjecture.** A minimizing graph separates the disk into connected regions. The paper proves the corresponding statement for three regions under the connectedness analysis developed there, while connectedness for general minimizing partitions remains open.
record.source_name: Antonio Cañete and Manuel Ritoré, “Least-perimeter partitions of the disk into three regions of given areas”, arXiv:math/0307207 (2003).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0307207

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2003). “The most interesting mathematical open question for these problems is to show that the minimizing configurations must have connected regions, either in $\rr^2$ or in the disk.”

record.title: Threshold existence conjecture for graph sequences
record.statement: Let ${\cal G}=\{G_1,\ldots,G_n,\ldots\}$ be a graph sequence, and let $th({\cal G})$ denote its threshold when one exists. **Threshold existence conjecture.** Every graph sequence ${\cal G}$ has a threshold $th({\cal G})$. The conjecture concerns the missing general existence theorem for pebbling thresholds; the supplied status evidence says this implication is false.
record.source_name: Glenn Hurlbert, “A Survey of Graph Pebbling”, arXiv:math/0406024 (2004).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0406024

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of June 2004). “Unfortunately, although seemingly intuitive, this implication is false.”

record.title: Karp's evasiveness conjecture for monotone graph properties
record.statement: Let a graph property be a partition of the unlabeled graphs on a fixed number of vertices into graphs with and without the property. The property is **monotone** if it is preserved under the removal of edges. Associate to it the simplicial complex whose vertices are graph edges and whose simplices are the graphs having the property. A simplicial complex is **nonevasive** if it is a point, or if it has a vertex whose link and deletion are both nonevasive; it is **evasive** if it is not nonevasive. **Karp's conjecture.** All nontrivial monotone graph properties are evasive. The conjecture concerns the decision-tree complexity of graph properties and has connections with combinatorial and algebraic topology. It was proved for a prime-power number of vertices and for $n=6$ by Kahn, Saks, and Sturtevant; the paper studies possible counterexamples for $n=10$.
record.source_name: Alexander Engström, “Transitive graphs in counterexamples to Karp's conjecture”, arXiv:math/0512421 (2005).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0512421

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2005).

record.title: Morris's conjecture on the threshold for 3-uniform FC-families
record.statement:
For integers $n\geqslant 4$, let $FC(3,n)$ denote the threshold quantity for 3-uniform families on an $n$-element ground set as defined in the paper. **Morris's conjecture.**

$$
FC(3,n)=\left\lfloor \frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor+1.
$$

The conjecture was suggested by the paper's discussion of known $FC$-families and is presented as an open direction following partial results.
record.source_name: Robert Morris, “FC-families, and improved bounds for Frankl's Conjecture”, arXiv:math/0702348 (2007).
record.references:

record.title: The $d$-step conjecture for simple polytopes
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a simple $d$-polytope with $2d$ facets, and let $u$ and $v$ be two **complementary vertices**, meaning vertices not lying in a common facet. **The $d$-step conjecture.** There is a path of length $d$ from $u$ to $v$.

This is the crucial $n=2d$ case underlying the Hirsch and non-revisiting conjectures. Its status is not established by the supplied source context.
record.source_name: Edward D. Kim and Francisco Santos, “An update on the Hirsch conjecture”, arXiv:0907.1186 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0907.1186

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2009). “Besides its implications in linear programming, which motivated the conjecture in the first place, it is one of the most fundamental open questions in polytope theory.”

record.title: Grünbaum’s face-width conjecture for cubic graphs on orientable surfaces
record.statement: **Conjecture 2.** For any embedding of a cubic graph in an orientable surface $S_g$ such that $\operatorname{ew}(G^*)\ge 3$, we have $\phi_c(G)=4$. Equivalently, every cubic graph embedded in $S_g$ with $\operatorname{fw}(G)\ge 3$ is three-edge-colourable. Here $\operatorname{fw}(G)$ is the least number of points in which a noncontractible curve in $S_g$ meets $G$, and, for cubic embedded graphs, $\operatorname{fw}(G)=\operatorname{ew}(G^*)$.
